questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: What is the primary focus of community health nursing?

choices.text: Providing specialised surgical treatment to individual patients
Promoting health and preventing illness among individuals, families and communities
Managing only patients admitted to hospitals
Providing medication without assessing community health needs

questions.rationale: Community health nursing focuses on health promotion, disease prevention, early identification of health problems and community-based care. Its approach considers the health needs of individuals, families and populations rather than concentrating exclusively on hospital treatment.

questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: Which development significantly strengthened the delivery of primary healthcare services in Ghana through community participation?

choices.text: The introduction of specialised surgical units
The implementation of the Community-based Health Planning and Services programme
The establishment of private pharmacies only
The expansion of hospital-based specialist clinics

questions.rationale: The Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) programme strengthened primary healthcare by bringing essential services closer to communities. It emphasises community participation, household-level care and collaboration between health workers and local structures.

questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: Which international declaration is historically associated with the global commitment to primary healthcare?

choices.text: Declaration of Alma-Ata, 1978
Geneva Convention, 1949
Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948
Ottawa Treaty, 1997

questions.rationale: The Alma-Ata Declaration of 1978 established primary healthcare as a key strategy for achieving health for all. It emphasised equitable access, community participation, intersectoral collaboration and appropriate technology.

questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of the Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) initiative in Ghana?

choices.text: To concentrate all healthcare services in regional hospitals
To improve access to essential primary healthcare through community-based service delivery
To replace all district hospitals with private clinics
To provide healthcare exclusively to government employees

questions.rationale: CHPS is a Ghanaian primary healthcare strategy designed to improve geographical access to essential health services. It promotes community ownership, household visits, preventive care and collaboration with community volunteers and leaders.

questions.topic: N&MC Code of Professional Conduct for CHNs
questions.question_text: Which statutory body regulates the nursing and midwifery professions in Ghana?

choices.text: Ghana Registered Nurses and Midwives Association
Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana
National Health Insurance Authority
Ghana Medical Association

questions.rationale: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (N&MC) is the statutory regulatory body established under Part III of the Health Professions Regulatory Bodies Act, 2013 (Act 857). It regulates professional standards, registration, licensing and disciplinary matters relating to nursing and midwifery.

questions.topic: N&MC Code of Professional Conduct for CHNs
questions.question_text: Which legislation establishes the Nursing and Midwifery Council as a statutory regulatory body in Ghana?

choices.text: National Health Insurance Act, 2012 (Act 852)
Health Professions Regulatory Bodies Act, 2013 (Act 857)
Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851)
Local Governance Act, 2016 (Act 936)

questions.rationale: The Health Professions Regulatory Bodies Act, 2013 (Act 857) provides the statutory framework for the Nursing and Midwifery Council. Section 54 identifies the Council's object as securing the highest standards of nursing and midwifery training and practice in the public interest.

questions.topic: N&MC Code of Professional Conduct for CHNs
questions.question_text: Which professional obligation requires a community health nurse to protect information obtained from patients during care?

choices.text: Confidentiality
Delegation
Advancement
Competition

questions.rationale: Confidentiality requires nurses to protect patients' personal and health information from unauthorised disclosure. Information should only be shared with appropriate persons when there is consent, a lawful basis or another recognised professional justification.

questions.question_text: Which ethical principle recognises a patient's right to make informed decisions about personal healthcare?

choices.text: Justice
Autonomy
Beneficence
Non-maleficence

questions.rationale: Autonomy recognises the individual's right to make voluntary and informed decisions about personal healthcare. Nurses should provide adequate information and respect competent patients' decisions, including decisions they may personally disagree with.

questions.question_text: The ethical principle of beneficence requires a community health nurse to:

choices.text: Avoid all interactions with patients
Act in ways that promote the wellbeing of patients and communities
Provide services only to individuals who can pay
Disclose every patient's health information publicly

questions.rationale: Beneficence means acting for the benefit of others and promoting their health and welfare. In community nursing, it includes health education, disease prevention, appropriate treatment and referral.

questions.question_text: Which ethical principle is primarily concerned with avoiding actions that cause unnecessary harm to patients?

choices.text: Justice
Autonomy
Non-maleficence
Fidelity

questions.rationale: Non-maleficence means avoiding or minimising harm to patients. Nurses apply this principle by practising within their competence, following safety procedures and avoiding interventions that expose patients to unnecessary risks.

questions.question_text: In community health nursing, the ethical principle of justice primarily requires:

choices.text: Providing fair and equitable healthcare without unjust discrimination
Giving priority to patients who are personally known to the nurse
Providing services only to patients with private insurance
Allowing community leaders to decide which patients deserve treatment

questions.rationale: Justice concerns fairness and equitable distribution of healthcare resources and services. Community health nurses should avoid discrimination based on factors such as ethnicity, religion, disability, gender or socioeconomic status.

questions.question_text: In nursing practice, negligence is best defined as:

choices.text: A deliberate refusal to follow a patient's cultural beliefs
Failure to exercise the reasonable standard of care expected in the circumstances, resulting in harm
Any disagreement between a nurse and a patient
The appropriate referral of a patient to a higher-level facility

questions.rationale: Negligence involves a failure to meet the applicable standard of reasonable care, resulting in foreseeable harm or injury. In a negligence claim, relevant issues include duty of care, breach, causation and damage.

questions.question_text: What is informed consent in healthcare?

choices.text: A patient's agreement obtained after receiving adequate information and understanding the proposed intervention
A nurse's decision to perform a procedure without discussing it with the patient
An agreement obtained through threats or intimidation
A relative's automatic approval of every procedure for a competent adult

questions.rationale: Informed consent is a voluntary decision made by a person with decision-making capacity after receiving relevant information about a proposed intervention. The patient should understand the purpose, material risks, benefits and reasonable alternatives before agreeing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a recognised right under Ghana's Patients' Charter?

choices.text: The right to receive care without any professional assessment
The right to information about one's health condition and proposed treatment
The right to demand any medication regardless of clinical indication
The right to access another patient's medical records without permission

questions.rationale: The Patients' Charter recognises patients' rights to relevant information about their health and care. This supports informed decision-making, participation in treatment and respectful communication between patients and healthcare professionals.

questions.topic: Scope of Practice for Community Health Nurses
questions.question_text: Which activity is consistent with the scope of practice of a Community Health Nurse in Ghana?

choices.text: Performing major surgery independently at a CHPS compound
Conducting child welfare services, health education and appropriate referrals
Prescribing every medicine without regard to professional authorisation
Providing specialist treatment outside the nurse's competence

questions.rationale: Community Health Nurses contribute to preventive, promotive and basic community-based healthcare. Their activities include child welfare services, health education, household visits, early identification of illness and referral within their authorised scope.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of maintaining professional boundaries during community home visits?

choices.text: To establish personal friendships with every household
To maintain a safe, respectful and professionally appropriate relationship with clients
To avoid communicating with family members
To encourage patients to depend entirely on the nurse

questions.rationale: Professional boundaries define appropriate limits in the nurse-client relationship. They protect patients from exploitation, preserve professional judgement and help maintain trust in healthcare delivery.

questions.topic: Advocacy and Whistleblowing in the Community
questions.question_text: What is patient advocacy in community health nursing?

choices.text: Supporting and protecting patients' rights, interests and access to appropriate healthcare
Making all healthcare decisions on behalf of patients
Promoting the personal interests of the nurse
Preventing patients from asking questions about their care

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy involves supporting patients to understand and exercise their rights and obtain appropriate care. It includes communicating concerns, promoting fair treatment and helping patients navigate healthcare services.

questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: A CHN is assigned to a rural community where many mothers do not attend child welfare clinics because of distance. Which action best reflects the historical and continuing primary healthcare approach in Ghana?

choices.text: Wait until mothers independently arrange transport to the district hospital
Organise community outreach and collaborate with local leaders to improve access to child welfare services
Discontinue child welfare services in the community
Restrict services to mothers who live near the health facility

questions.rationale: Community outreach is consistent with the primary healthcare approach and the objectives of CHPS. Working with local leaders and community structures helps reduce barriers to essential preventive services.

questions.topic: N&MC Code of Professional Conduct for CHNs
questions.question_text: A CHN is asked by a community leader to disclose the HIV status of a resident to encourage others to avoid contact with the person. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Disclose the person's HIV status because the leader requested it
Protect the patient's confidentiality and provide general HIV education without identifying the individual
Post the patient's status on the community noticeboard
Discuss the patient's status with all household members without consent

questions.rationale: A patient's HIV status is confidential health information and must not be disclosed simply because a community leader requests it. The nurse can address stigma and transmission concerns through non-identifying health education while following applicable legal and public health requirements.

questions.topic: N&MC Code of Professional Conduct for CHNs
questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse realises that a clinical procedure requested by a family is beyond the nurse's competence and authorised scope of practice. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Perform the procedure to avoid disappointing the family
Explain the limitation, seek appropriate professional assistance and arrange referral where necessary
Ask an untrained family member to perform the procedure
Perform the procedure without documenting it

questions.rationale: Nurses are accountable for practising within their competence and authorised scope. Seeking assistance and referring appropriately protects patient safety and prevents unauthorised practice.

questions.topic: N&MC Code of Professional Conduct for CHNs
questions.question_text: A CHN discovers that a colleague has recorded a home visit that was never conducted. What is the most professionally appropriate response?

choices.text: Ignore the matter because the colleague is experienced
Follow the appropriate reporting procedures and ensure that records are accurate
Alter the record to make it appear that the visit occurred
Publicly insult the colleague in the community

questions.rationale: Falsifying clinical or service records undermines professional integrity and may compromise patient care and accountability. The nurse should document facts accurately and report the concern through the appropriate supervisory or institutional channels.

questions.question_text: A competent adult patient refuses a recommended treatment after the nurse has explained its benefits and risks. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Force the patient to accept treatment
Respect the informed decision, document the discussion and explain available alternatives
Threaten to withdraw all future healthcare services
Ask a community leader to overrule the patient's decision

questions.rationale: A competent adult has the right to make informed decisions about personal healthcare, including refusing treatment. The nurse should respect autonomy, ensure that the patient understands the consequences and document the decision appropriately.

questions.question_text: A CHN has limited quantities of essential health supplies for a community outreach programme. Which action best demonstrates the ethical principle of justice?

choices.text: Reserve all supplies for families personally known to the nurse
Allocate available supplies fairly according to clinical need and approved criteria
Give supplies only to people who offer gifts
Distribute supplies randomly without considering health needs

questions.rationale: Justice requires fair and equitable allocation of limited healthcare resources. Clinical need, vulnerability and approved service criteria should guide decisions rather than personal relationships or financial influence.

questions.question_text: A nurse notices that a community volunteer is using an unsterilised instrument during wound care. Which ethical principle is most directly threatened?

choices.text: Non-maleficence
Autonomy
Justice
Fidelity

questions.rationale: Using unsterilised instruments can expose patients to infection and preventable harm. The nurse should intervene to stop the unsafe practice and ensure that wound care follows appropriate infection prevention procedures.

questions.question_text: A nurse administers the wrong medication to a patient during a home visit and immediately recognises the error. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Hide the error to avoid disciplinary action
Assess the patient, take immediate steps to minimise harm and seek appropriate clinical assistance
Alter the medication record to show the correct medicine
Wait until the next scheduled visit to assess the patient

questions.rationale: The immediate priority after a medication error is patient safety and the prevention of further harm. The nurse should obtain appropriate clinical assistance, report the incident through established procedures and document the facts accurately.

questions.question_text: A competent patient refuses to sign a consent form for a proposed procedure. The nurse believes the procedure is beneficial. What is the correct action?

choices.text: Obtain the patient's thumbprint without permission
Respect the refusal, explore the patient's concerns and inform the responsible clinician
Ask a neighbour to sign on the patient's behalf
Proceed because the nurse believes the procedure is necessary

questions.rationale: A competent patient's refusal must be respected, even when the healthcare professional believes treatment would be beneficial. The nurse should clarify concerns, provide relevant information and communicate the decision to the responsible clinician.

questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse observes signs suggesting that a child may be experiencing physical abuse. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Ignore the findings because the matter is a private family issue
Ensure the child's immediate safety, document objective findings and report through appropriate child protection channels
Confront the suspected perpetrator violently
Share the child's identity and allegations on social media

questions.rationale: Suspected child abuse requires a safeguarding response that prioritises the child's safety and follows applicable reporting procedures. Documentation should be factual and objective, and information should be shared only with appropriate authorities or professionals.

questions.question_text: A nurse conducts a home visit and enters a patient's bedroom without permission, although the patient is conscious and able to decide. Which professional concern is most directly involved?

choices.text: Violation of privacy and respect for the patient's dignity
Appropriate delegation
Improved interprofessional collaboration
Continuing professional development

questions.rationale: Patients have a right to privacy and respectful treatment during healthcare encounters. A nurse should seek permission before entering private spaces or undertaking care, except where an emergency or other lawful justification applies.

questions.question_text: A patient complains that a nurse spoke disrespectfully to her because she is unable to pay for a service immediately. Which right under the Patients' Charter is most relevant?

choices.text: The right to respectful and non-discriminatory treatment
The right to demand employment from the health facility
The right to select the nurse's personal beliefs
The right to access confidential information about other patients

questions.rationale: The Patients' Charter supports dignity, respect and equitable treatment in healthcare. A patient's financial circumstances should not justify humiliating or discriminatory conduct by a healthcare worker.

questions.question_text: A patient asks a CHN to explain the purpose and possible side effects of a prescribed medicine. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Tell the patient not to ask questions about prescribed treatment
Provide accurate information within the nurse's competence and clarify any uncertainties with the prescriber
Give the patient information obtained from an unrelated patient's record
Refuse to explain because only doctors can communicate with patients

questions.rationale: Patients have a right to relevant information about their care and treatment. Nurses should communicate accurately within their competence and seek clarification when a question requires information beyond their professional knowledge.

questions.topic: Scope of Practice for Community Health Nurses
questions.question_text: A CHN identifies a pregnant woman with severe headache, blurred vision and elevated blood pressure during a community visit. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Advise the woman to rest at home and return after one week
Recognise possible severe pre-eclampsia and arrange urgent referral for appropriate assessment and management
Recommend herbal treatment and avoid referral
Wait for the next routine antenatal clinic before taking action

questions.rationale: Severe headache, visual disturbance and elevated blood pressure during pregnancy may indicate pre-eclampsia with severe features. The nurse should prioritise maternal and fetal safety and arrange urgent referral rather than attempting management beyond the nurse's authorised capacity.

questions.topic: Scope of Practice for Community Health Nurses
questions.question_text: A CHN identifies a patient with persistent chest pain and difficulty breathing at a community outreach session. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Provide routine health education and ask the patient to return next month
Assess immediate danger, provide appropriate first aid within competence and arrange urgent referral
Prescribe long-term cardiac medication without assessment
Ask the patient to walk home for further observation

questions.rationale: Persistent chest pain with breathing difficulty may indicate a life-threatening emergency. The nurse should rapidly assess the patient, provide emergency support within competence and arrange prompt transfer to an appropriate facility.

questions.topic: Scope of Practice for Community Health Nurses
questions.question_text: A community health nurse is organising a health education session on cholera prevention. Which activity best reflects the nurse's public health role?

choices.text: Educating households on safe water, hand hygiene, food hygiene and early reporting of symptoms
Treating all community members with antibiotics regardless of symptoms
Advising residents to avoid reporting diarrhoeal illness
Restricting health education to patients already admitted to hospital

questions.rationale: Community health nurses play an important role in preventing communicable diseases through health education and community mobilisation. Safe water, sanitation, hand hygiene and early identification of suspected cases help reduce cholera transmission.

questions.question_text: A family visited by a CHN offers the nurse an expensive gift in appreciation for providing routine healthcare. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Accept the gift because it is a sign of respect
Politely decline the gift in accordance with professional and institutional rules
Accept the gift and promise preferential treatment
Demand a more expensive gift before continuing care

questions.rationale: Accepting expensive gifts may create conflicts of interest, expectations of preferential treatment or exploitation of the professional relationship. The nurse should follow institutional policy and maintain impartiality.

questions.question_text: A patient sends a CHN repeated personal messages on social media unrelated to healthcare. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Develop a romantic relationship with the patient
Maintain professional communication boundaries and redirect necessary communication to approved channels
Share the patient's messages publicly
Provide the patient with personal financial information

questions.rationale: Professional boundaries apply to digital communication as well as face-to-face interactions. Nurses should use appropriate communication channels, protect confidentiality and avoid relationships that may compromise professional judgement.

questions.question_text: A CHN visits a household and is asked by the family to keep a large amount of money for safekeeping. What is the best response?

choices.text: Accept the money as part of the home visit
Politely decline and explain that handling the family's personal money is outside the professional role
Accept the money and use it to purchase personal items
Ask the family to pay the nurse for the visit

questions.rationale: Handling a patient's or family's money for personal safekeeping is outside the usual professional responsibilities of a community health nurse. Declining such arrangements helps prevent financial disputes, exploitation and conflicts of interest.

questions.topic: Advocacy and Whistleblowing in the Community
questions.question_text: A CHN discovers that a child with a disability is repeatedly excluded from community health activities because of discrimination. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Accept the exclusion as a community tradition
Advocate for inclusive access and work with caregivers and community leaders to address barriers
Advise the family to stop using healthcare services
Share the child's personal information publicly to attract attention

questions.rationale: Advocacy requires nurses to support equitable access to healthcare and challenge discriminatory practices. Working with families and community structures can improve inclusion while protecting the child's dignity and privacy.

questions.topic: Advocacy and Whistleblowing in the Community
questions.question_text: A nurse notices that a community health facility has no functioning handwashing station, creating an infection prevention risk. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Ignore the situation because facility resources are not a nursing concern
Report the safety concern through appropriate channels and advocate for corrective action
Continue all procedures without hand hygiene
Blame patients for the facility's inadequate infrastructure

questions.rationale: Nurses have a professional responsibility to promote patient safety and identify preventable risks in healthcare environments. Reporting the problem and advocating for corrective action supports infection prevention and quality improvement.

questions.topic: History of Community Health Nursing in Ghana
questions.question_text: A district health team wants to improve immunization coverage in a remote community where residents rarely visit the health facility. Which strategy best reflects the principles of CHPS?

choices.text: Wait for residents to travel to the district hospital
Engage community leaders, organise outreach services and involve community volunteers in mobilisation
Restrict immunization to children whose parents are employed
Stop immunization activities until a new hospital is constructed

questions.rationale: CHPS promotes community participation and delivery of essential services close to where people live. Community mobilisation and outreach can reduce geographical and social barriers to immunization.

questions.question_text: A nurse conducts a home visit and documents that a patient has a fever, although the nurse did not measure the patient's temperature. What is the most appropriate professional concern?

choices.text: The nurse has demonstrated accurate documentation
The nurse has recorded an unverified finding as an objective measurement
The nurse has appropriately delegated responsibility
The nurse has protected the patient's confidentiality

questions.rationale: Professional documentation must be accurate, objective and based on observations or reliable information. The nurse should distinguish between measured findings, patient-reported symptoms and clinical interpretations.

questions.question_text: A patient who is registered with the National Health Insurance Scheme is asked to pay an unauthorised fee for a covered service. The patient seeks assistance from the CHN. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Tell the patient to pay without asking questions
Help the patient understand the appropriate complaint process and direct the concern to the responsible facility or NHIA channel
Promise that every service is free regardless of NHIS benefit rules
Advise the patient to stop using all health services

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy includes helping individuals understand their healthcare entitlements and seek clarification about disputed charges. The nurse should not make unsupported promises about coverage but should guide the patient to the appropriate facility or NHIA complaint process.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse is conducting an HIV education programme. A participant asks a question that reveals a misunderstanding about HIV transmission. Which response best demonstrates beneficence and respect for persons?

choices.text: Ridicule the participant for having incorrect information
Provide accurate, respectful information and allow participants to ask further questions
Ignore the question to avoid embarrassment
Identify people living with HIV in the community as examples

questions.rationale: Health education should promote wellbeing while respecting the dignity of participants. Accurate and non-judgemental communication helps correct misconceptions without exposing individuals to stigma or discrimination.

questions.topic: N&MC Code of Professional Conduct for CHNs
questions.question_text: A CHN is asked to sign a clinical record prepared by another worker, but the nurse has not verified the information. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Sign immediately because the other worker is trusted
Review and verify the information before signing or decline to authenticate information that cannot be confirmed
Sign using another nurse's name
Destroy the record without reporting the concern

questions.rationale: A nurse is professionally accountable for information authenticated by their signature. Records should be checked for accuracy, and a nurse should not knowingly certify information that has not been verified.

questions.topic: Scope of Practice for Community Health Nurses
questions.question_text: During a household visit, a CHN identifies a patient with signs of a possible stroke, including sudden facial weakness and difficulty speaking. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Advise the patient to sleep and review the condition the following day
Recognise a possible stroke, assess immediate safety and arrange urgent transfer to an appropriate facility
Provide a routine appointment at the next monthly outreach
Give food and drink to test swallowing ability

questions.rationale: Sudden facial weakness and speech difficulty are warning signs of stroke, which requires urgent medical assessment. The nurse should avoid delaying referral and should not give oral food or fluids when swallowing may be impaired.

questions.question_text: During a home visit, a nurse is invited to participate in a family dispute unrelated to the patient's care. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Take sides and use professional authority to threaten one family member
Remain professionally neutral and redirect the discussion to the purpose of the visit or appropriate support services
Use the disagreement to obtain personal information about the family
Promise to resolve the dispute personally

questions.rationale: A home visit should maintain a clear professional purpose and appropriate boundaries. The nurse may identify health or safeguarding concerns and refer the family to suitable support services without becoming personally involved in the dispute.

questions.topic: Advocacy and Whistleblowing in the Community
questions.question_text: A nurse witnesses a colleague demanding money from patients before providing a service that should be delivered without such payment. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Remain silent because the colleague is senior
Document the concern objectively and report it through the appropriate institutional or regulatory channels
Join the colleague to avoid conflict
Publish unverified accusations on social media

questions.rationale: Demanding unauthorised payments may constitute professional misconduct and undermine equitable access to healthcare. Reporting through appropriate channels supports accountability while reducing the risks associated with public disclosure of unverified allegations.

questions.question_text: A nurse is providing care to an unconscious adult who has no available representative, and immediate intervention is necessary to prevent serious harm. Which legal and ethical concept generally supports emergency care in this situation?

choices.text: Implied consent in an emergency
Financial consent
Retrospective punishment
Professional privilege

questions.rationale: When a patient lacks decision-making capacity and urgent treatment is necessary to prevent serious harm, emergency care may generally proceed under the principle of implied consent or emergency necessity. The intervention should be limited to what is reasonably necessary, with appropriate documentation and subsequent communication.

questions.question_text: A CHN is distributing a limited number of mosquito nets. A community leader insists that his relatives should receive the nets first, although several households have more vulnerable children. Which response best addresses the ethical dilemma?

choices.text: Distribute the nets to the leader's relatives to maintain good relations
Apply transparent, need-based criteria that prioritise vulnerable households
Give all nets to the households closest to the CHPS compound
Cancel the distribution programme

questions.rationale: The ethical principle of justice requires fair allocation based on relevant health needs rather than personal influence. Transparent criteria help protect vulnerable groups and maintain public trust in community health services.

questions.topic: N&MC Code of Professional Conduct for CHNs
questions.question_text: A CHN posts a photograph of a patient receiving treatment during a home visit on a personal social media account. The patient's face and address are visible, and no consent was obtained. Which professional obligation has been most clearly breached?

choices.text: Confidentiality and protection of patient privacy
Continuing professional development
Appropriate delegation
Community mobilisation

questions.rationale: The photograph reveals identifiable health and personal information without the patient's permission. Nurses must protect confidentiality and comply with professional and institutional rules governing patient images and digital communication.

questions.question_text: A nurse fails to refer a patient with clear signs of severe respiratory distress despite recognising the seriousness of the condition. The patient subsequently suffers serious harm. Which elements would be particularly relevant in assessing a possible negligence claim?

choices.text: Duty of care, breach of the required standard, causation and damage
The patient's occupation and political affiliation only
The nurse's popularity in the community
Whether the patient's family agrees with the nurse personally

questions.rationale: A negligence claim generally examines whether a duty of care existed, whether the standard of care was breached, whether that breach caused the harm and whether legally recognised damage occurred. Failure to arrange an appropriate referral may be relevant to the breach and causation elements.

questions.question_text: A 16-year-old patient tells a CHN that an adult has sexually abused them and begs the nurse not to tell anyone. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Promise absolute secrecy and take no further action
Explain the limits of confidentiality, prioritise immediate safety and follow child protection reporting procedures
Confront the alleged perpetrator without considering the child's safety
Tell the child that the disclosure is not a healthcare concern

questions.rationale: A disclosure of sexual abuse involving a minor requires a safeguarding response and appropriate reporting through established child protection channels. The nurse should explain that confidentiality has limits where protection from abuse is required and should avoid actions that could expose the child to further harm.

questions.question_text: A competent patient refuses to allow a nurse to discuss the patient's diagnosis with relatives. The relatives insist that they must be informed because they provide financial support. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Disclose the diagnosis because relatives are paying for care
Respect the patient's decision and maintain confidentiality unless a valid legal or other recognised exception applies
Give the relatives access to the entire medical record
Ask the community chief to decide whether disclosure is necessary

questions.rationale: A competent patient generally controls who receives personal health information. Financial support or family relationships do not automatically authorise disclosure, although lawful exceptions may apply in specific circumstances.

questions.topic: Scope of Practice for Community Health Nurses
questions.question_text: A CHN is working at a CHPS compound when a patient develops a condition requiring specialist investigation and treatment unavailable at that level. The patient asks the nurse to manage the condition locally to avoid transport costs. What is the best professional decision?

choices.text: Attempt specialist treatment despite lacking the necessary competence and resources
Explain the need for higher-level care, provide appropriate stabilisation within competence and facilitate referral
Discharge the patient without explanation
Ask an unqualified volunteer to provide specialist treatment

questions.rationale: A CHN must recognise the limits of the facility's resources and the nurse's competence. Appropriate stabilisation and timely referral protect patient safety while maintaining continuity of care.

questions.question_text: A CHN regularly visits a patient with a chronic illness. The patient begins relying on the nurse for personal financial assistance and asks the nurse to borrow money on the patient's behalf. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Borrow money for the patient to strengthen the relationship
Maintain professional boundaries, explain the limits of the nursing relationship and refer the patient to appropriate social support
Stop all nursing care immediately without arranging continuity
Use the patient's situation to request money from other patients

questions.rationale: The nurse should not allow the therapeutic relationship to become a personal financial arrangement. Maintaining boundaries while connecting the patient with appropriate social support protects both the patient and the professional relationship.

questions.topic: Advocacy and Whistleblowing in the Community
questions.question_text: A nurse reports suspected diversion of essential medicines through the approved reporting channel. The nurse's supervisor threatens to transfer the nurse for raising the concern. What is the most appropriate next step?

choices.text: Withdraw the report immediately to avoid disagreement
Preserve relevant factual records and seek guidance through appropriate higher-level or protected reporting mechanisms
Destroy all evidence to protect colleagues
Publish patients' confidential records online to prove the allegation

questions.rationale: Whistleblowing involves reporting suspected wrongdoing or risks through appropriate channels in the public interest. The nurse should maintain factual documentation, protect confidential information and seek guidance on applicable reporting and protection procedures.

questions.question_text: During an outbreak, a patient with a suspected highly infectious disease refuses recommended isolation. The patient is competent and insists on returning to a crowded household. Which response best balances autonomy and the duty to protect public health?

choices.text: Physically restrain the patient without legal authority
Explain the risks, explore voluntary measures and follow applicable public health procedures for managing the risk
Ignore the risk because autonomy always overrides public health protection
Publicly announce the patient's identity and diagnosis

questions.rationale: Autonomy is important, but it may be subject to lawful public health measures when an individual's actions create a serious risk to others. The nurse should use the least restrictive appropriate approach, provide clear information and follow applicable legal procedures.

questions.question_text: A nurse is conducting a home visit when a family refuses entry because they believe the visit is unnecessary. There is no known emergency or legal authority permitting entry. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Force entry because the nurse has a professional identification card
Respect the refusal, explain the purpose of the visit and arrange another suitable contact if appropriate
Threaten the family with arrest
Enter through another door without permission

questions.rationale: A routine home visit does not give a nurse automatic authority to enter a private residence against the occupants' wishes. The nurse should respect privacy, communicate professionally and follow appropriate procedures if a genuine safeguarding or emergency concern exists.

questions.topic: Advocacy and Whistleblowing in the Community
questions.question_text: A CHN identifies a community where children with disabilities are unable to access immunization because the outreach site has steps and no accessible route. What is the most appropriate advocacy response?

choices.text: Accept the barrier because outreach services are not required to accommodate disability
Raise the accessibility concern and work with the health team and community to provide an inclusive alternative
Tell caregivers to stop bringing children for immunization
Provide immunization only to children who can enter the site independently

questions.rationale: Equitable healthcare requires identifying and reducing barriers that exclude people with disabilities. Advocacy may involve modifying the outreach venue, arranging accessible services or providing an appropriate alternative delivery approach.
